speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're presenting with significant constitutional symptoms and a palpable lymph node. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have experienced any cough, shortness of breath, or chest pain recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any swelling or pain in your abdomen or groin area, and do you have a history of recent travel or exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of smoking, or have you experienced any difficulty swallowing or breathing due to the neck swelling? I would also like to examine the texture and mobility of that supraclavicular node more closely.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of a fixed, painless supraclavicular lymph node and abdominal fullness is highly suggestive of a malignancy, likely originating in the gastrointestinal tract. I will request an abdominal CT scan and a biopsy of the lymph node to confirm the source of the cancer.
